description: The machine-readable form of the evidence bundle that orcinus-verify returns for a change. It is the structured version of the prose bundle in skills/orcinus-verify/SKILL.md. A bundle is only as strong as its revision binding: every check runs on the bundle revision, so a PASS cannot be carried from one revision to another; the fail-first proof records the pre-fix run separately. A bundle whose overall verdict is PASS must have no check with verdict FAIL or INCOMPLETE and no non-empty unverified_items; anything else is INCOMPLETE or FAIL. Validate with skills/orcinus-verify/scripts/validate_evidence.py (standard library only).

acceptance_criteria.description: The acceptance criteria. If there are none, the verification must stop (INCOMPLETE), not invent them.

cwd.description: The directory the command ran in.

exit_code.description: The real exit code. 0 means the command succeeded; a non-zero code is a FAIL, not a pass.

stdout_artifact.description: Where the stdout is saved (a path, relative to the bundle).

tool_version.description: The version of the tool that ran (for example 'pytest 8.4.2').

unverified_items.description: What this check could not establish. Non-empty means the check is INCOMPLETE, not PASS.

verdict.description: The verdict for this check alone.

dirty_files.description: Uncommitted files, required when working_tree_state is 'dirty', empty otherwise.

fail_first.description: The fail-first proof (orcinus-verify step 3): the new test failed on the pre-fix code and passes after it.

failed_before.description: True when the test was shown failing on the pre-fix code.

method.description: How the pre-fix run was done: a separate git worktree (preferred), a revert at the smallest possible scope, or not-applicable when the change has no behaviour to test (say why in the note).

note.description: Why the method was chosen, or why fail-first does not apply.

passed_after.description: True when the same test passes after the fix.

test.description: The test that proves the behaviour (for example 'test_capture_persian_only').

files_changed.description: Every file the change touched. A file outside the requested scope is a finding, not a detail.

findings.description: Findings, each with file, line, and evidence. A blocking finding makes the overall verdict FAIL.

evidence.description: The behaviour that proves the finding (a command, an output, or a file).

requirement.description: The requirement as the verifier understood it, in their own words.

reviewer_identity.description: Who verified — the verifier, never the implementer. A name, a session id, or an agent id.

revision.description: The exact commit the checks ran on (full or abbreviated SHA), or 'working-tree' with the state in working_tree_state. A PASS is bound to this revision only.

schema_version.description: The schema version. Bump it when a required field is added or a rule changes.

unresolved_risks.description: Risks that remain after the change (for example 'the 3.9 matrix has never run in CI').

unverified_items.description: What could not be checked, and why. Non-empty means the overall verdict cannot be PASS.

verdict.description: The overall verdict. PASS requires every check PASS, no blocking findings, and no unverified items. FAIL means a blocking finding. INCOMPLETE means a check could not run or evidence is missing.

working_tree_state.description: 'clean' (no uncommitted changes) or 'dirty'. If 'dirty', dirty_files must list the uncommitted files.

verification_plan.description: The plan the verification was run against: the change type, the gates this change had to pass, and the gates that do not apply, each with a reason. A bundle whose verdict is PASS needs this plan, and every required gate needs a passing check with the same name.

change_type.description: What kind of change was verified (for example 'bug-fix', 'docs-only', 'refactor').

not_applicable_gates.description: Gates this change does not need, each with a reason.

required_gates.description: The gates this change had to pass, by the exact check name that proves each one.

title: ORCINUS verification evidence bundle
